analysis.title: GOAL: Global Opportunity Asset Locator: Giving credit to balance — bonds gradually moving from headwind to hedge
key_insights: GS shifts back to overweight equities on a 3m horizon (in line with 12m). Earnings growth remains supportive and the valuation de-rating since the summer improves asymmetry into Q3 earnings season.
GS shifts to overweight bonds on a 12m horizon and stays neutral on a 3m horizon. Tactically it prefers shorter-duration fixed income and shifts to overweight cash for 3m.
GS shifts back to underweight credit for 3m, in line with 12m. It prefers equities over credit because spreads are tight relative to all-in yields and face releveraging and supply headwinds.

Global equities have been range-bound since summer despite strong earnings, and have de-rated alongside rising bond yields. Pressure is concentrated in small and mid caps, real estate, infrastructure and bond-proxy sectors.
The bond sell-off has been led by front-end and real yields rather than steeper curves, term premia or breakevens. Market pricing is more hawkish than the GS economists' baseline.

Markets price more than three further Fed hikes, at least two from the ECB and nearly four from the BoE. GS economists expect only one more hike each from the ECB and BoE, with potential cuts starting next year.
The macro baseline is a Goldilocks-like backdrop: resilient growth, low US recession risk, inflation momentum moderating into 2027. GS says this is more favourable for 60/40 portfolios.
GS's dynamic asset allocation model signals less downside risk for 60/40 portfolios over the next 12 months. The model does not capture AI capex earnings tailwinds and may understate equity upside.
The Risk Appetite Indicator fell to zero from elevated levels over two weeks. The RAI PC2 'Monetary Policy' factor is at one of its lowest levels since 2000, comparable to 2022.
Across 11 RAI PC2 troughs since 2000, the S&P 500 typically corrected before resuming its uptrend and US 10-year yields stayed rangebound over the following 12 months. The exception was 2022.
Higher starting yields give long-duration bonds better asymmetry over longer horizons: potential gains from rate relief now exceed likely losses from a further rise in yields.
Yield increases above two standard deviations over three months have historically been hard on equity returns. Equities can buffer higher yields when earnings growth is strong.
MSCI AC World 12-month forward P/E has fallen nearly 20% year to date, an unusually large late-cycle de-rating. Valuation compression is largest in technology, especially hardware.
The USD IG credit spread accounts for only 15% of the yield, versus a 45% recent average. Credit spreads are close to the credit team's year-end targets, with risks tilted toward more widening.
GS prefers USD over EUR credit and has shifted to neutral on IG versus HY. It prefers HY to leveraged loans and agency MBS to IG, and is underweight EUR AT1s versus HY.

Commodities stay neutral. Dec26 Brent has stayed above $100/bbl with more Iranian attacks on tankers, even though Persian Gulf oil exports are back to pre-war levels. GS lowered its year-end gold target to $4,650/toz from $4,900/toz.

The GS commodities team recommends hedging geopolitical risk through long 2027 positions in European gasoline. It sees TTF gas reaching 150 EUR/MWh by year-end if Persian Gulf LNG exports do not improve and the winter is colder than average.

Hedging view: cross-asset implied vol is low (VIX at 15) and implied correlations are near historical lows because of high dispersion. Upside equity hedges and call options are inexpensive. GS favours VIX call spreads, front-end receiver swaptions and EUR/USD and EUR/CHF puts.
The MOVE-to-VIX ratio is at its highest since 2024. GS would tactically sell payers on back-end rates to fund equity puts.

GS's US team expects S&P 500 earnings growth of 11% in 2027 and 2028, and 18% in 2027 excluding revaluation of equity stakes. Companies are described as 'over-earning' from private stake gains and semiconductor and memory margin expansion.

sector_views.rationale: Part of a barbell with rate-sensitive stocks. Tech has been supported by strong earnings growth even as valuations de-rated.

sector_views.sector: Rate-sensitive, low-vol, high-dividend and bond-proxy equities
sector_views.rationale: These have de-rated since the summer and could benefit from eventual rate relief.
Noted as having suffered drawdowns since the summer from rising yields. GS includes selective rate-sensitive names in its barbell but gives no standalone sector stance.

earnings_insights: GS expects Q3 earnings seasons to surprise to the upside in both the US and Europe.

The US team expects 18% S&P 500 earnings growth in 2027 excluding 'other income' from revaluation of equity stakes. It expects 11% growth in both 2027 and 2028 including base effects. These are GS estimates, not reported figures.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Yields are driven by front-end and real yields. GS forecasts 4.74% in 3m, 4.64% in 6m and 4.45% in 12m.
Implies yield declines of 49bp, 59bp and 78bp, supporting the 12m overweight in US bonds.
GS expects energy prices to normalise into year-end. The forecast path is the basis for easing inflation momentum.

macro_indicators.reading: 11% in 2027 and 2028; 18% in 2027 excluding equity stake revaluation
macro_indicators.interpretation: Earnings growth is outstripping nominal GDP by one of the widest gaps since the 1980s.
Market pricing is more hawkish than GS economists' baseline, which supports a view that front-end rates are skewed to the downside.
Close-to-trend growth with a stable labour market and low recession risk.
Year-end target was cut from $4,900 on a more hawkish Fed weighing on ETF demand. Central bank diversification remains the structural driver.

trade_ideas.description: Buy call options to add selectively to equity exposure while holding tactical cash
trade_ideas.rationale: Equity volatility is anchored by high dispersion, which makes call exposure inexpensive.
trade_ideas.risk: Rates volatility, Middle East tensions and midterm election uncertainty.

trade_ideas.description: Buy 3m VIX call spreads as broad downside hedge into year-end
trade_ideas.rationale: Max-payoff ratios are high relative to history and a macro shock could lift correlations sharply.
trade_ideas.risk: Dispersion keeps the VIX low if no broad shock occurs.

trade_ideas.description: Buy front-end receiver swaptions (12m 25-delta receiver on 1y or 2y USD rates) as a recession hedge
trade_ideas.rationale: Front-end forward rates have risen sharply YTD, and receivers benefit from the central-bank put and from rate relief if energy prices fall.

trade_ideas.description: Buy puts on EUR/USD and EUR/CHF to hedge Euro area fiscal risk
trade_ideas.rationale: A targeted hedge against rising Euro area sovereign risk premia.
trade_ideas.risk: Less likely to pay off unless sovereign stress broadens across the region.

trade_ideas.description: Sell payers on back-end rates to fund equity puts
trade_ideas.rationale: Further sharp rate rises would weigh more on equities than bonds, and rates volatility is elevated relative to equity volatility.

trade_ideas.description: Long 2027 positions in European gasoline to hedge geopolitical risk
trade_ideas.rationale: Refined products remain near YTD highs and the commodities team sees continued supply risk.

risk_factors: Higher rates and energy prices are the main near-term downside risk to equities.
US midterm election uncertainty could lift equity volatility from current low levels.
Fiscal concerns, AI capex financing needs and capital competition add uncertainty around fair value for bond yields.
Credit spread risks to GS forecasts are tilted toward more widening, with continued supply and releveraging.
Euro area sovereign stress, particularly France, could spread across the region.
Concerns about the durability of AI infrastructure earnings have weighed on valuations. A broader de-risking in Tech would hit the barbell.
Persian Gulf LNG disruption and a colder-than-average winter could push TTF gas to 150 EUR/MWh.
The GS model may understate equity upside because it does not capture AI capex earnings.
charts_described: Exhibit 22 shows the simulated PnL of a 12m 25-delta receiver on 1y or 2y USD rates against a put on the S&P 500 at current market prices, with US recession periods shaded. The text says the receiver would have delivered a larger payoff than an out-of-the-money S&P 500 put in previous recessions.
Exhibit 8 shows the RAI PC2 'Monetary Policy' factor at one of its lowest levels since 2000.
Exhibit 15 shows global equities de-rated materially, with 12m forward P/E ratios down 20%.
vol_and_positioning: VIX is at 15. FX volatility is similarly anchored. Credit implied vol has picked up but is low relative to history.

Implied correlations are close to historical lows both within and across S&P 500 sectors, because of high dispersion. This keeps index volatility contained and makes equity upside hedges inexpensive, particularly in rate-sensitive areas.
Rates volatility has risen sharply, pushing the MOVE-to-VIX ratio to its highest since 2024, though it has started to reset recently.
VIX call spreads look attractive as broad downside hedges into year-end, with max-payoff ratios high relative to history. VIX is also low relative to CDS spreads.
Front-end receiver swaptions are a more convex recession hedge. In past recessions a receiver swaption on short-dated rates would have paid more than an out-of-the-money S&P 500 put.
Positioning in equities has declined since the summer, which GS says improves asymmetry.
geopolitical: Middle East tensions, including Iranian attacks on tankers, keep Brent above $100/bbl for Dec26 futures.
Persian Gulf oil exports (including 'dark exports') are back to pre-war levels, but Persian Gulf LNG exports have not improved, which is the risk behind the TTF 150 EUR/MWh scenario.
US midterm election uncertainty is expected to raise equity volatility from current low levels.
Euro area sovereign risk repricing, particularly French OAT spreads, produced a safety bid for US Treasuries, German bunds and UK gilts.

tension_points.bull_case: Higher carry and reinvestment yields cushion further rate rises, inflation is normalising and energy prices are expected to peak. Potential gains from rate relief now exceed likely losses, so bonds should move from headwind to hedge over 12 months.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher yields, fiscal concerns, AI capex capital competition and inflation uncertainty argue for tactical caution. Additional duration may add volatility rather than cushion portfolios in the near term.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A continued sharp rise in yields of more than two standard deviations over three months, which has historically pressured equities, and energy-price volatility that keeps central banks hawkish.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong earnings growth and the de-rating improve asymmetry. Equities have buffered higher yields, and rate relief could allow valuation expansion.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher rates and energy prices remain the main downside risk, and the Tech-led earnings base could be hit by AI infrastructure durability concerns.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further sharp increases in yields, or a broader de-risking in Tech stocks.
